title: Pure core, imperative shell
summary: Put decisions in pure functions and keep side effects in a thin outer shell.

steps.title: Pure functions
body: 1. its result depends only on its arguments, and
2. it has no side effects (no I/O, no changing shared state).
Pure functions are the easiest code there is to test: call with values, compare the result. No setup, no fakes, no cleanup. They are also easy to reason about and safe to reuse.

steps.title: Functional core, imperative shell
body: Structure a feature in two layers:
- **Core**: pure functions that make every decision. Given the current state and an input, return the new state and *what should happen*.
- **Shell**: thin, boring code that gathers inputs (clock, files, user), calls the core, and carries out the side effects.
failures + 1 >= max ? new(true, "Account locked") : new(false, $"{max - failures - 1} tries left");
All the interesting logic is tested with plain values. The shell is so simple it barely needs testing.

steps.title: Extract the core
prompt: `Thermostat.Tick` mixes reading a sensor, deciding, and switching a heater. Extract the decision into a pure static function:
`static string Decide(double current, double target)` returns `heat` when `current` is more than 0.5 below `target`, `cool` when more than 0.5 above, and `idle` otherwise.
`Tick` should then just read, call `Decide`, and act. The tests call `Decide` with plain numbers.
starter: class Thermostat(Func<double> readSensor, Action<string> setHeater, double target)
solution: class Thermostat(Func<double> readSensor, Action<string> setHeater, double target)
public static string Decide(double current, double target)
template: Dojo.Eq("Tick still drives the heater", new List<string> { "heat" }, dojoSet);

forbid.message: Decide does not touch the sensor or heater

steps.title: A pure state machine
prompt: Write the pure core of a vending machine. No I/O, no mutation:
- `static class Vending` with `static (Machine Next, string Output) Handle(Machine m, string command)`:
- `buy` with credit >= 2 and stock > 0: credit -2, stock -1, output `vend`
solution: public static (Machine Next, string Output) Handle(Machine m, string command) => command switch
"buy" when m.Credit >= Price && m.Stock > 0 => (m with { Credit = m.Credit - Price, Stock = m.Stock - 1 }, "vend"),
template: Dojo.Eq("the input is not mutated", new Machine(5, 5), dojoBefore);
